I notice that the X*Mod on M (a3) is not significant (p = 0.077), but the confidence interval for this  [-0.008,  -0.001]
Furthermore, I also noticed that the indirect effect is not significant (at any levels of the moderator).

How should I interpret this? I was thinking of removing X*Mod on M from the model... but then 0.07 is not that far from significant (and looking at the CI...)?
The indirect effect is not significant... When I remove this interaction (X*Mod on M) and calculate the indirect effect as a1*b1, the indirect effect is even less significant (p=0.104).
I am totally lost on what it means that the indirect effect is not significant. Does that mean that there is no real mediation effect?


Many thanks!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Indirect effect: not significant, CI does not contain zero
parts: I notice that the X*Mod on M (a3) is not significant (p = 0.077), but the confidence interval for this  [-0.008,  -0.001]
p values based on the Wald z statistic are calculated from the SE, assuming the sampling distribution is symmetric.  Bootstrap CIs are not necessarily symmetric.
Does that mean that there is no real mediation effect?

When there is a moderator, you don't make a blanket statement that there is no mediation for anyone.  You need to make that statement (and test it) separately for different meaningful levels of the moderator.
